newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore must keep competitive edge - president.
newsitem.headline: Singapore must keep competitive edge - president.

text.p: Singapore President Ong Teng Cheong said on Monday the republic must stay ahead of fierce competition now emerging in areas where it has traditional been strong.

In a speech to open the first parliamentary session after the general election in January, Ong said Singapore's neighbours were seeking high quality investments in port, airport and financial services -- niches it has long occupied.
Ong said he welcomed fair market competition because it would spur the republic to improve and stay ahead, cooperating with its neighbours even as it competed.
"Economic growth need not be a zero sum game, as it expands the pie for all," Ong said, adding, however, that the challenge was formidable because competition was now tougher.
He said that Singapore had a diversified and globalised economy with strong links to countries in the region and beyond.
"We are not overexposed or vulnerable to problems with any one economic partner," Ong said.
He noted Singapore had put aside sizeable reserves during years of high growth as a buffer for difficult times.
The president, in his opening address, also stressed the need for investing in education and upgrading infrastructure to meet competition and the population's changing needs.
